text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - State-owned energy utility Slovenske Elektrarne (SE) is seeking an average energy price increase of 25 percent by the end of this year. SE said delays in the price hike is costing it some 100 million crowns a month.
- Economics Minister Karol Cesnek said it would be premature to talk about the extent of an energy price increase, but that he would welcome a concrete proposal for a price hike as soon as possible.

- The central bank said mergers of the two largest financial institutions, commercial bank VUB and savings bank Slovenska Sporitelna, was at a purely hypothetical level, as no one has presented a concrete plan for such a move.
- Parliament on Wednesday approved an opposition proposal to oblige the government to present its strategy and projects for privatisation of two largest commercial banks, VUB and IRB.
- Some 71 percent of Slovaks support the country's integration into the European Union, while only nine percent would be against the move.
- Slovakia's major plastic pipe producer, Plastika Nitra, has called a regular shareholders meeting for April 18.
NARODNA OBRODA - Parliamnet will begin its next regular sesion on March 18. The preliminary agenda includes no major economic items.
- The Bratislava plant of the German car producer Volkswagen expects 1996 production to total 18 billiom crowns.
- VW's Slovak unit completed 6,706 Golf model cars in the first two months of this year, and at the same time produced 49,215 gear boxes and 998,568 components for gear boxes.

SME - Opposition parties plan to ask Parliamentary Chairman Ivan Gasparovic to call an extraordinary session, where they will demand the dismissal of Culture Minister Ivan Hudec and Interior Minister Gustav Krajci.

- State-run Slovak Railways (ZSR) said it plans to reduce its workforce by some 10,000 people, some 20 percent of its overall number of employees, this year. ZSR however, said it would only lay off some 5,000 people, and the remaining 5,000 will be transfered to its daughter companies.
- The ruling Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS) has cancelled bilateral talks with the opposition Party of the Democratic Left (SDL).
